content.title: Images Need the Right Text Story
content.hook: An image can carry information, add decoration, or act as part of another control. The useful question is not “What is the image?” but “What information does the user need from it?”
content.context: An image can carry information, add decoration, or act as part of another control. The useful question is not “What is the image?” but “What information does the user need from it?”
goals: Choose useful alternative text for informative images and recognize when an image should be decorative instead.

content.question: A page shows a graph whose main point is “Sign-ups increased 32% this month.” What kind of alternative text is useful?

options.text: Text that communicates the important information shown by the graph
Leave the image without any plan

feedback.correct: Useful alternative text communicates the purpose or important information of an informative image.
feedback.incorrect: Useful alternative text communicates the purpose or important information of an informative image.

content.question: A page has a purely decorative divider image that adds no information. What is the better approach?

options.text: Write a long description of the divider
Treat it as decorative so it does not add irrelevant noise
Put the same paragraph beside it

feedback.correct: Not every image needs meaningful descriptive text. Decorative images should not create unnecessary information for someone using the page.
feedback.incorrect: Not every image needs meaningful descriptive text. Decorative images should not create unnecessary information for someone using the page.

content.title: Write for purpose
content.text: Alternative text should be concise enough to use but rich enough to preserve the important information. Do not describe every visual detail when those details do not matter to the task.

content.question: A developer writes alt="beautiful blue graph with three lines and tiny dots" for a chart whose only task-relevant fact is the 32 percent increase. What is wrong?

options.text: It describes visual details instead of communicating the useful information.
The browser ignores all image text.

feedback.correct: Alternative text should preserve the information the image contributes to the task.
feedback.incorrect: Alternative text should preserve the information the image contributes to the task.

activities.title: Tiny lab
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt: Pick three images from a sample page: one informative, one decorative, and one that acts as a link. Decide what a user needs to know for each before writing any text.
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.
content.sampleResponse: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.

feedback.correct: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.
feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

content.question: What is the first question to ask when writing image text?

options.text: How many pixels wide is the image?
What information or purpose does the image provide?
Can I use the longest sentence possible?

feedback.correct: Purpose comes first. The wording follows the purpose.
feedback.incorrect: Purpose comes first. The wording follows the purpose.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Mental model: Alternative text is a bridge for information, not a caption contest.
Senior habit: Describe the meaning the image contributes, not everything the eye can see.
